summary: Two-party consent mechanism

ai.s: Adds a two-party consent layer to AI Notes recordings: an environment acknowledgement for the initiator and tiered consent or notification for the recipient, with a full audit trail.
ai.pr: AI Notes recorded conversations with no recipient consent, no private-setting check, no real-time recording indicator and no consent audit trail.
ai.wy: Compliance: IMEX GDPR requirements and German recording law (§201 StGB) require informed consent and per-recording awareness.
ai.oc: Specified: once-per-event initiator acknowledgement, Tier 1 full consent and Tier 2 lightweight notification for recipients, a persistent recording indicator and consent audit logging.

summary: Data deletion access

ai.s: Gives AI Notes recipients a way to have their recordings deleted and defines what server-side deletion and data retention must cover.
ai.pr: Only the initiator could delete a recording, server-side deletion scope was ambiguous, and there was no defined retention period or disclosure for AI Notes data.
ai.wy: Compliance: GDPR Articles 17 and 5(1)(e), raised under the IMEX GDPR requirements.
ai.oc: Specified: a recipient deletion route (self-service or DSAR), removal of audio, transcript, summary, metadata and cached outputs, preserved consent audit logs, and a defined, disclosed retention policy.

summary: Admin Panel Scope Restriction

ai.s: Lets organisers restrict AI Notes to all badge scans, scheduled meetings only or specific attendee types, enforced in the app and on the server.
ai.pr: AI Notes had a single on/off toggle, so when enabled it was available for every badge scan, including open floors and hallways with higher bystander risk.
ai.wy: Compliance and client request: IMEX preferred limiting AI Notes to scheduled meetings to reduce GDPR risk.
ai.oc: Specified: per-event scope settings for admins, the Record button hidden for non-qualifying scans and server-side rejection of non-qualifying uploads.

summary: Show notification bubble on mobile app

ai.s: Shows numeric unread badges on the mobile app icon so attendees and exhibitors notice messages, meeting requests and schedule changes, with an opt-out setting.
ai.pr: The mobile app had no visual indicator of unread or pending items, so Busworld attendees and exhibitors were missing messages and meeting requests.
ai.wy: Client request from Busworld 2027, which runs as an ongoing community on the mobile app.
ai.oc: Specified: real-time app-icon badge counters capped at 99+, a default-on settings toggle stored server-side, independent of push notifications.

summary: Move require section to the server side (useRedirectByRequirements)

ai.s: Moves the profile-requirements redirect to the server so users with incomplete profiles are redirected before the page renders, removing a visible flash.
ai.pr: useRedirectByRequirements ran client-side after hydration, so the requested page briefly rendered before redirecting and the logic depended on hydrated Redux state.
ai.wy: Technical debt: the hook carried a TODO to move server-side, and the flash hurts user experience.
ai.oc: Specified: server-side redirects to /profile/edit or /profile/video, preserved on-page toast behaviour and removal of client router-based redirect logic.

summary: Hash check in integration update flow considers inactive AccountEvents

ai.s: Fixes the integration update hash check so previously deactivated visitors and exhibitors are reactivated when their data is reprocessed.
ai.pr: The hash check matched against inactive AccountEvents rows, threw DataUnchangedException and skipped the update, so deactivated entities were never reactivated.
ai.wy: Data integrity in integration imports: re-sent records must restore event participation.
ai.oc: Suggested fix: hash checks use active-only AccountEvents and skip comparison when none exists, letting the update proceed.

summary: Organizer toggle to enable feedback form and create report

ai.s: Adds an organiser toggle to switch on mobile-app event feedback collection and a downloadable Event Feedback report of submissions.
ai.pr: Event feedback was being built into the mobile app, but there was no way to store submissions, let organisers turn collection on or off, or report on it.
ai.wy: Part of Attendance & Event Analytics 2026, giving organisers attendee feedback data.
ai.oc: Specified: an off-by-default Event Feedback toggle after OTP Authentication that flags the app, stored submissions, and a report with rating, text, timestamp, name, email and role.

summary: Client Manager: Event Organizer can view correct Active Accounts metrics in the Visitor List so that Event data is not misrepresented

ai.s: Makes the Client Manager Visitor List distinguish active team members from total active accounts so event participation metrics are not misrepresented.
ai.pr: The Visitor List's Active Accounts metric blurred team members and total active accounts, misleading organisers about participation.
ai.wy: Accurate event participation reporting for organisers, under Attendance & Event Analytics 2026.
ai.oc: Specified at user-story level; the definition of an active attendee or team member is out of scope.
